arxiv-1701-08277.title: Dominant Majorana bound energy and critical current enhancement in ferromagnetic-superconducting topological insulator
arxiv-1701-08277.creator: M. Khezerlou, H. Goudarzi, S. Asgarifar
arxiv-1701-08277.description: Abstract Among the potential applications of topological insulators, we theoretically study the coexistence of proximity-induced ferromagnetic and superconducting orders in the surface states of a 3-dimensional topological insulator. The superconducting electron-hole excitations can be significantly affected by the magnetic order induced by a ferromagnet.

arxiv-1707-01355.title: Align and Copy: UZH at SIGMORPHON 2017 Shared Task for Morphological Reinflection
arxiv-1707-01355.creator: Peter Makarov Tatiana Ruzsics Simon Clematide
arxiv-1707-01355.description: Abstract This paper presents the submissions by the University of Zurich to the SIGMORPHON 2017 shared task on morphological reinflection. The task is to predict the inflected form given a lemma and a set of morpho-syntactic features. We focus on neural network approaches that can tackle the task in a limited-resource setting.

arxiv-1905-02651.title: Comparing Image Quality in Phase Contrast sub μ \mu X-Ray Tomography - A Round-Robin Study
arxiv-1905-02651.creator: S. Zabler, M. Ullherr, C. Fella, R. Schielein, O. Focke, B. Zeller-Plumhoff, P. Lhuissier, W. DeBoever, R. Hanke
arxiv-1905-02651.description: Abstract Abstract How to evaluate and compare image quality from different sub-micrometer (sub \mu ) CT scans? A simple test phantom made of polymer microbeads is used for recording projection images as well as 13 CT scans in a number of commercial and non-commercial scanners.

arxiv-2012-09962.title: Addressing Feature Suppression in Unsupervised Visual Representations
arxiv-2012-09962.creator: Tianhong Li, Lijie Fan, Yuan Yuan, Hao He, Yonglong Tian, Rogerio Feris, Piotr Indyk, Dina Katabi
arxiv-2012-09962.description: Abstract Contrastive learning is one of the fastest growing research areas in machine learning due to its ability to learn useful representations without labeled data. However, contrastive learning is susceptible to feature suppression – i.e., it may discard important information relevant to the task of interest, and learn irrelevant features.

arxiv-2102-00112.title: Neutron-Induced, Single-Event Effects on Neuromorphic Event-based Vision Sensor: A First Step Towards Space Applications
arxiv-2102-00112.creator: SETH ROFFE 1, HIMANSHU AKOLKAR 2 , ALAN D. GEORGE 1 , BERNABÉ LINARES-BARRANCO 5 , AND RYAD BENOSMAN. 2, 3, 4
arxiv-2102-00112.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the suitability of neuromorphic event-based vision cameras for spaceflight, and the effects of neutron radiation on their performance. Neuromorphic event-based vision cameras are novel sensors that implement asynchronous, clockless data acquisition, providing information about the change in illuminance greater than ( ≥ 120 ​ d ​ B ) (\geq 120dB) with sub-millisecond temporal precision.

arxiv-2107-08636.title: Mixed spin S=1 and S=½ layered lattice in Cu 2 F 5
arxiv-2107-08636.creator: Dmitry M. Korotin, Dmitry Y. Novoselov, Vladimir I. Anisimov, Artem R. Oganov
arxiv-2107-08636.description: Abstract The electronic and magnetic structure, including the Heisenberg model exchange interaction parameters, was explored for the recently proposed novel cuprate Cu 2 F 5 . Using the DFT+U calculation, it is shown that the compound is formed by two types of copper ions with d 9 d^{9} and d 8 d^{8} electronic configurations.

arxiv-2112-06298.title: Unveiling the underlying interactions in Ta 2 NiSe 5 from photo-induced lifetime change
arxiv-2112-06298.creator: Denis Golež, Sydney K. Y. Dufresne, Min-Jae Kim, Fabio Boschini, Hao Chu, Yuta Murakami, Giorgio Levy, Arthur K. Mills, Sergey Zhdanovich, Masahiko Isobe, Hidenori Takagi, Stefan Kaiser, Philipp Werner, David J. Jones, Antoine Georges, Andrea Damascelli, Andrew J. Millis
arxiv-2112-06298.description: Abstract We present a generic procedure for quantifying the interplay of electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in photo-doped insulators through a comparative analysis of theoretical many-body simulations and time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) of the transient response of the candidate excitonic insulator Ta 2 NiSe 5 . Our analysis demonstrates that the electron-electron interactions dominate the electron-phonon ones.

arxiv-2304-00031.title: Coherent radio bursts from known M-dwarf planet host YZ Ceti
arxiv-2304-00031.creator: J. Sebastian Pineda, Jackie Villadsen
arxiv-2304-00031.description: Abstract Observing magnetic star-planet interactions (SPI) offers promise for determining magnetic fields of exoplanets. Models of sub-Alfvénic SPI predict that terrestrial planets in close-in orbits around M dwarfs can induce detectable stellar radio emission, manifesting as bursts of strongly polarized coherent radiation observable at specific planet orbital positions.

arxiv-2312-03949.title: Product Formula of Artin Symbols in Non-abelian Extensions
arxiv-2312-03949.creator: Sosuke Sasaki
arxiv-2312-03949.description: Abstract . The product formula of Artin symbols (norm residue symbols) is an important equality that connects local and global class field theory. Usually, the product formula of Artin symbols is considered in abelian extensions of global fields. In this paper, however, the product is considered in non-abelian extensions such that each symbol is well-defined.

arxiv-2402-02649.title: Densely Decoded Networks with Adaptive Deep Supervision for Medical Image Segmentation
arxiv-2402-02649.creator: Suraj Mishra, Danny Z. Chen
arxiv-2402-02649.description: Abstract Medical image segmentation using deep neural networks has been highly successful. However, the effectiveness of these networks is often limited by inadequate dense prediction and inability to extract robust features. To achieve refined dense prediction, we propose densely decoded networks ( D ​ D ​ N {D\!D\!N} ), by selectively introducing ‘crutch’ network connections.

arxiv-2407-04660.title: COBRA: Optimal Factorization of Cosmological Observables
arxiv-2407-04660.creator: Thomas Bakx, Nora Elisa Chisari, Zvonimir Vlah
arxiv-2407-04660.description: Abstract We introduce COBRA (Cosmology with Optimally factorized Bases for Rapid Approximation), a novel framework for rapid computation of large-scale structure observables. COBRA separates scale dependence from cosmological parameters in the linear matter power spectrum while also minimising the number of necessary basis terms N b N_{b} , thus enabling direct and efficient computation of derived and nonlinear observables.

arxiv-2503-10659.title: MARRO: M ulti-headed A ttention for R hetorical Ro le Labeling in Legal Documents
arxiv-2503-10659.creator: Purbid Bambroo, Subinay Adhikary, Paheli Bhattacharya, Abhijnan Chakraborty, Saptarshi Ghosh, Kripabandhu Ghosh
arxiv-2503-10659.description: Abstract Identification of rhetorical roles like facts, arguments, and final judgments is central to understanding a legal case document and can lend power to other downstream tasks like legal case summarization and judgment prediction. However, there are several challenges to this task.

britannica-1911-rope-walking.title: Rope-walking (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rope-walking.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rope-walking.description: Article 'Rope-walking' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. tricks of equilibrium on a rope or wire stretched between two supports. It has been popular with most Asiatic and European peoples from the beginning of history. Before the middle of the 19th century a rope was invariably used, and was stretched as tightly as possible, on which account the art was called Tight-rope Walking.

pmc-10698440.title: Immunotherapy in SMARCB1 (INI-1)-deficient sinonasal carcinoma: Two case reports
pmc-10698440.creator: Lu Zhang, Ai-Xin Gao, Yu-Lu He, Ming-Jin Xu, Hai-Jun Lu
pmc-10698440.description: BACKGROUNDSMARCB1/INI-1 deficient sinonasal carcinoma (SDSC) is a rare subset of sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma with a poor prognosis. Here, we present two case reports of SDSC patients. We also review the literature on this tumor. This is the first published report of SDSC treatment with immunotherapy.

pmc-11691709.title: IMPACT OF FRAILTY AND DEMENTIA ON REHABILITATION OUTCOMES IN OLDER ADULTS SURGICALLY TREATED FOR HIP FRACTURE
pmc-11691709.creator: Giulia Caggiu, Matteo Monzio Compagnoni, Patrizia Floris, Martina Manna, Francesco De Filippi, Michela Passamonte, Paolo Mazzola
pmc-11691709.description: We investigated the impact of frailty and dementia on rehabilitation outcomes after hip fracture (HF) surgery in an Italian Orthogeriatric Unit (OGU). We prospectively enrolled all patients aged ≥70 years admitted to the OGU at Sondrio Hospital (Italy) in 2011-2019, with HF requiring surgery. We administered a comprehensive geriatric assessment, including factors related to fracture and surgery.

pmc-12456028.title: Evaluation of vision transformers for the detection of fullness of garbage bins for efficient waste management
pmc-12456028.creator: Parakram Singh Tanwer, Shishir Maheshwari, Sushree Behera, Amit Chauhan, T. Sunil Kumar
pmc-12456028.description: Efficient waste management is crucial for urban environments to maintain cleanliness, reduce environmental impact, and optimize resource allocation. Traditional waste collection systems often rely on scheduled pickups or manual inspections, leading to inefficient resource utilization and potential overflow issues. This paper presents a novel approach to automate the detection of garbage container fullness from images using machine learning techniques.

pmc-13246093.title: Global temporal trends and projections for the incidence of chlamydial infection among women of childbearing age over the next decade
pmc-13246093.creator: Yutong Kang, Xuanming Xu, Chenyang Zhao, Qiheng Yuan, Yanying Feng, Meiqin Zheng, Zhenjun Li, Yajie Wang
pmc-13246093.description: Women of childbearing age (WCBA) are at unreasonable risk of excruciating pregnancy-related complications associated with chlamydial infection, constituting a paramount peril to global public health. This study aims to demonstrate the temporal tendencies of chlamydial infection in WCBA and prognosticate its future incidence, providing momentous illumination for precise prevention and management blueprints.

pmc-13389459.creator: Alessia di Lillo, Sara Tavella, Fabio Iannelli, Giovanni Crisafulli, Ubaldo Gioia, Lucrezia A. Trastus, Matteo Cabrini, Fabrizio d’Adda di Fagagna
pmc-13389459.description: The DNA damage response is a complex network of pathways that cells activate to safeguard genome integrity following DNA damage, including DNA double-strand breaks. We and others previously reported that RNA polymerase II, together with components of the preinitiation complex, is recruited to exposed DNA ends.

pmc-13472166.title: Severe aortic regurgitation revealing Takayasu arteritis: a case report
pmc-13472166.creator: Fatima Ezzahra Dommane, Meryem Haboub, Mohamed Khaldi, Abdenasser Drighil
pmc-13472166.description: BackgroundTakayasu arteritis (TA) is a rare chronic autoimmune vasculitis affecting large and medium-sized arteries, mainly in young women, and is more common in Asia. It may cause stenosis, occlusions, aneurysms, aortic dilation, and aortic valve disease. We are reporting a rare case of severe aortic valve insufficiency and aortic dilation in the context of TA.

pmc-13689456.title: Phage-first treatment results in subpopulation-driven collateral sensitivity to beta-lactams in an extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-13689456.creator: Claire Han, Karishma Patel, Haoran Gao, Jacob T. Sanborn, Thomas D. Nguyen, Jack F. Klem, Brian M. Ho, Patrick D. Kenney, Yanan Zhao, Troy D. Wood, Dwayne R. Roach, Liang Chen, Nicholas M. Smith
pmc-13689456.description: Nosocomial Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections are among the most challenging infections to treat, and resistance to last-line agents, including polymyxins and aztreonam-based therapies, risks a future with limited or no clinical treatment options. Bacteriophages (phages) have emerged as a promising therapeutic option, both in cocktails and when given in combination with antibiotics.
